name: The Fall of Bramblehaven

casualties.attackers: Heavy — multiple squads wiped during wall breaches
casualties.defenders: Near-total (survivors executed on Captain Toadette's standing orders)

summary: The Fall of Bramblehaven was a brutal day-long siege where Captain Toadette's Peach Loyalist forces absolutely demolished a Fawful-held bastion. Waluigi wasn't there—nobody INVITED Waluigi—but even from a distance this one sent chills down Waluigi's magnificent spine. The no-prisoners policy cemented Toadette as the scariest person in the Mushroom Kingdom, and Waluigi does NOT say that lightly because Waluigi has arm-wrestled Bowser.
description:
Waluigi wants to start by saying he has no love for Fawful. Fawful is a cackling gremlin who talks about himself in the third person, which Waluigi finds deeply irritating for reasons he cannot fully explain. BUT what Captain Toadette did at Bramblehaven makes Fawful look like a preschool bully by comparison. This battle is the reason Waluigi sleeps with one eye open whenever the Loyalists are mentioned.

Toadette's forces had been camping in the hills for two days before the assault. Scouts from the garrison spotted the campfires but apparently nobody thought 'hey, maybe we should tell someone about the ARMY sitting on our doorstep.' Whether that was incompetence or sabotage, Waluigi doesn't know. What Waluigi DOES know is that if HE had been running that garrison, there would have been a proper watch rotation. Waluigi is VERY good at staying awake all night because Waluigi has trust issues developed over a LIFETIME of being underestimated.

The dawn assault hit from three directions simultaneously because Toadette doesn't believe in doing things halfway. She's like Waluigi in that respect, except Waluigi channels his intensity into SPORTS and SHOWMANSHIP, not into executing prisoners of war.

**Phase 1: The Breach**
The eastern wall came down in two hours. Loyalist sappers had tunneled under it OVERNIGHT—while the garrison was sleeping—and packed the foundation with explosives. WAH! That's actually terrifying when you think about it. Imagine going to sleep knowing there's an enemy army nearby, and while you're dreaming about whatever Fawful's goons dream about, someone is digging UNDER YOUR BED and filling the basement with bombs.

The detonation buried an entire defensive squad alive. Loyalist infantry poured through before the dust settled because Toadette apparently thinks things like 'waiting for visibility' are for people who aren't FANATICALLY DEVOTED to Princess Peach.

The western and northern breaches took longer and cost the Loyalists dearly. Crossbow fire, boiling oil—the garrison fought HARD on those walls. Toadette reportedly executed one of her own sergeants for suggesting they pull back from the northern approach. She EXECUTED her own soldier for recommending a tactical retreat. Waluigi has coached sports teams with more compassion than this woman commands an army.

**Phase 2: Street Fighting**
Once inside, the battle turned into a street-by-street nightmare. Fawful's troops knew the layout and used it cleverly—collapsing buildings to create chokepoints, flooding intersections with alchemical smoke, rigging doorways with spring-loaded traps. Smart tactics! Waluigi respects smart tactics! The Loyalists lost entire squads to ambushes in the market district, which proves that determination without intelligence gets you killed.

But Toadette just kept feeding reinforcements through the breaches. She had numbers and she had zealotry, and in urban warfare those two things together are nearly impossible to stop. Waluigi knows this from extensive experience with Mario Party board games, where sheer stubbornness beats skill about sixty percent of the time and it makes Waluigi FURIOUS.

**Phase 3: The Keep**
By late afternoon, the fighting was pushed back to the central keep. The garrison commander—whose name was NEVER recovered from any surviving records, which Waluigi finds deeply suspicious because the Iron Legion documents people's LUNCH ORDERS but somehow nobody wrote down this person's name—made a final stand with about forty troops.

They barricaded the keep entrance and held for nearly three hours. THREE HOURS against an army. That's determination. That's grit. Waluigi respects that deeply. When the Loyalists finally broke through using a battering ram improvised from a market stall beam, the fighting inside was hand-to-hand. Close quarters. The kind of fighting where everyone gets bloody and nobody comes out feeling good about it.

**Phase 4: No Quarter**
This is where Waluigi stops making jokes.

Fifteen garrison troops tried to surrender. They put down their weapons. They raised their hands. They gave up.

Toadette's standing orders were clear: no prisoners from Fawful's forces. The surrendering troops were executed in the keep's courtyard. Some individual Loyalist soldiers reportedly hesitated or refused, which tells Waluigi that even fanatics have lines—they just got overruled by officers who didn't.

By nightfall, Bramblehaven was silent.

Waluigi has done a lot of questionable things in his life. He's cheated at tennis. He's rigged go-kart races. He once stole Luigi's hat just to see the look on his face. But there are LINES, and killing people who have surrendered is so far past the line that the line is a DOT. Captain Toadette scares Waluigi, and Waluigi is not someone who scares easily. Waluigi once played a horror board game and didn't flinch ONCE. Okay, maybe once. The point stands.

The intelligence recovered from the garrison was apparently valuable—troop movements, supply chains, communications with Fawful's command. So the Loyalists got what they came for. Whether it was WORTH what they did to get it is a question that Waluigi thinks has a pretty obvious answer, but Waluigi has been told his moral opinions are 'surprisingly nuanced for someone who once tried to monetize standing in a doorway,' so take that for what it's worth.
aftermath: Bramblehaven gave the Peach Loyalists a strategic foothold and a pile of intelligence. The prisoner executions drew condemnation from almost every faction—even groups nominally allied with the Loyalists were privately horrified. But here's the thing that makes Waluigi's stomach turn: it WORKED. Two subsequent Fawful garrisons surrendered without fighting rather than face the same fate. They surrendered to OTHER factions, mind you—nobody wanted to surrender to Toadette, for obvious reasons—but the fear accomplished what diplomacy couldn't. Fawful's territorial integrity in the Mushroom Kingdom was shattered. He had to abandon smaller outposts that were immediately grabbed by opportunistic local factions. The balance of power shifted, though whether it shifted toward anything resembling PEACE is a question Waluigi suspects the answer to is 'no.' WAH.

summary: Waluigi was not at this summit, which means Waluigi watched the coverage from a safe distance and screamed at the equivalent of a television for THREE CONSECUTIVE HOURS. The Second Diplomatic Summit produced the Mushroom Kingdom Disaster Relief Program—eight nations signed binding agreements, ships actually launched, refugees received actual aid, and real LOGISTICS happened instead of just handshakes and empty promises. That is a WIN. That is what MATTERS. But does anyone talk about that? NO. They talk about King Dedede turning a multilateral forum into a one-penguin therapy session that lasted longer than some theatrical productions. They talk about Lanky Kong getting BAITED into slapping a Kremling operative on camera after being systematically provoked by intelligence professionals. They talk about Prince Peasley's supply mission getting intercepted by Fawful's forces and twisted into a corruption scandal that cost him his title. They talk about FIVE DELEGATIONS walking out in sequence like they had choreographed it in advance. Waluigi calls this a 'qualified success that everyone will remember as a failure,' which is the WORST kind of success because you do not even get CREDIT for it. Waluigi knows this feeling INTIMATELY. WAH.
description:
Waluigi needs to walk through this disaster piece by piece because everyone is drawing the WRONG conclusions and it is giving Waluigi a stress headache that interferes with his tennis practice. The Second Summit was simultaneously the most productive and most chaotic diplomatic event of the current crisis, and people keep focusing on the chaos while ignoring the productivity. This is typical. This is how Waluigi's entire life works. Waluigi wins a tennis match through superior skill and strategy, and everyone talks about the one time Waluigi's racket flew out of his hand and hit a referee. PRIORITIES, people.

## What Actually Worked — The Part NOBODY Mentions

The summit opened stronger than the first one, which Waluigi has documented elsewhere and which was basically a potluck where everyone brought optimism and nobody brought a plan. Daisy hosted competently—tighter security protocols, broader attendance from regional powers, an actual AGENDA with time allocations and speaking orders instead of 'let's all be friends and see what happens.' Waluigi respects an agenda. Waluigi LIVES by agendas. Waluigi once created a seventeen-page tournament schedule with contingencies for weather, equipment failure, and Wario deciding to eat the prize money instead of competing for it.

The core achievement happened EARLY in the proceedings, before everything went sideways: the Mushroom Kingdom Disaster Relief Program. Eight nations signed binding commitments. Not 'agreed in principle.' Not 'expressed interest in further discussions.' Not 'promised to circle back after consulting domestic stakeholders.' SIGNED. With PENS. On PAPER that had legal force. Supplies began moving IMMEDIATELY. Ships launched from multiple ports. Refugees who had been waiting for aid since the Planar Fracture finally received tangible assistance.

This was not symbolic diplomacy designed to produce photographs for newsletters. This was LOGISTICS. Waluigi respects logistics more than almost anything because Waluigi has DONE logistics. Waluigi has organized doubles tennis tournaments with Wario as his partner, which requires coordinating equipment transport when your partner keeps 'accidentally' selling the spare rackets to fund garlic purchases. Waluigi has managed supply chains under pressure. Waluigi has learned that good intentions without operational infrastructure produce nothing except warm feelings and empty warehouses.

The crucial thing that everyone keeps MISSING in their hot takes and opinion pieces: the relief program survived EVERYTHING that followed. Delegations walked out in dramatic fashion. Reputations burned publicly and spectacularly. Social media commentary melted into a puddle of bad takes and worse analysis. And through all of it, the ships kept sailing. The supplies kept moving. The aid kept arriving at refugee camps that did not care about diplomatic scandals because they needed FOOD and MEDICINE and SHELTER.

THAT is the difference between performative diplomacy and functional diplomacy. The first summit was a group project where everyone received participation trophies and felt good about themselves. The second summit was a group project where the actual essay got written and submitted on time even though three people had a fistfight in the library, someone set off the fire alarm, and one group member gave a forty-five minute presentation about how great they personally are.

## The Dedede Detonation — A Study in Self-Immolation

Waluigi has complained about many things in his life. Waluigi has given SPEECHES about his grievances at sporting events, award ceremonies, and one memorable incident at a go-kart track that resulted in a temporary restraining order that Waluigi maintains was COMPLETELY UNJUST. But Waluigi has never—NEVER—done what King Dedede did at this summit.

Dedede did not merely give a long speech. Politicians give long speeches. That is EXPECTED and budgeted for in agenda planning. Dedede did not merely brag about Dreamland's contributions to regional stability. Monarchs brag about their kingdoms. That is TRADITIONAL and generally tolerated within reasonable limits. What Dedede did was VIOLATE THE BASIC SOCIAL CONTRACT OF MULTILATERAL DIPLOMACY.

The word MULTILATERAL contains hints about its meaning. It has LATERAL in it, implying SIDES. PLURAL. Multiple parties with different interests attempting to find common ground. Dedede treated the summit like a press conference about himself that happened to have a captive audience who could not change the channel without causing a diplomatic incident.

He began by listing everything Dreamland had done to support regional stability, which would have been acceptable if he had stopped at five minutes. He continued by implying that other nations were ungrateful for Dreamland's generosity, which crossed from acceptable into uncomfortable. He escalated by making it PERSONAL, criticizing specific delegations by name for insufficient appreciation of Dreamland's magnificence, which violated diplomatic norms that exist specifically to prevent this kind of public humiliation. And he kept GOING. And GOING. And GOING.

Waluigi has watched Wario eat an entire buffet in one sitting—appetizers through desserts, including the decorative ice sculpture that was not technically food but which Wario consumed anyway—and THAT took less time than Dedede's speech. Waluigi has played tennis matches that went to multiple tiebreakers that took less time than Dedede's speech. Waluigi has experienced waits at government bureaucracy offices that took less time than Dedede's speech, and those waits included the clerk taking a lunch break in the middle of processing Waluigi's paperwork.

The DK Crew walkout was not impulsive. It was STRUCTURALLY INEVITABLE given the conditions Dedede created. Once Dedede crossed from 'policy disagreement expressed through diplomatic channels' into 'personal humiliation of attendees broadcast to observers,' someone was going to leave. The social contract had already been violated. Remaining in the room meant accepting continued violation. DK happened to be the delegation with the lowest tolerance for penguin-shaped arrogance, but if DK had not walked out, someone else would have within minutes.

Waluigi RESPECTS DK for this decision. Waluigi has walked out of events for less significant provocations. Waluigi once walked out of a tennis award ceremony because they mispronounced his name THREE TIMES in succession and then gave the runner-up trophy to Luigi by mistake. Walking out when your dignity is being systematically attacked is not weakness. It is self-respect. Dedede forced everyone present to choose between self-respect and diplomatic protocol, and that is a choice no host should ever impose on their guests.

## The Cascade Failure — How One Exit Became Five

Once DK left, the summit entered what Waluigi recognizes from sports psychology as 'cascade failure.' It functions like a team sport where one player makes a critical error and instead of the team recovering through compensatory performance, everyone else starts making errors too because the collective VIBE has shifted from 'we can do this' to 'everything is falling apart.' Confidence is contagious. So is its absence.

One walkout made the next walkout psychologically easier. The taboo had already been broken. The precedent existed. Each subsequent walkout lowered the barrier for the next one, until five delegations had departed and the remaining attendees were looking at each other like survivors of a shipwreck wondering who was going to start building a raft and whether the remaining materials were even sufficient.

Rogueport withdrew its delegation, citing 'fundamental concerns about forum integrity.' The Piantas left with expressions of 'deep disappointment' that diplomatic translation conventions prevented from being more colorfully phrased. Isle Delfino departed amid 'reassessment of participation protocols.' The Noki Commonwealth exited quietly, which was somehow more damning than the dramatic walkouts because it suggested they had simply given up on the entire enterprise.

These departures were not primarily about Lanky's incident with the Kremling operative. They were not even primarily about Dedede's speech, although that was the proximate cause. They were about NORMS collapsing. The unwritten social agreement that says 'we stay even when it is uncomfortable because leaving makes it worse' had evaporated the moment Dedede proved that staying was ALSO going to be uncomfortable. If enduring discomfort no longer provided benefits, why endure it?

Daisy cut Dedede's microphone eventually. This was CORRECT. This was the RIGHT call that should have been made forty minutes earlier. But it was too late because the damage was already airborne and spreading. You cannot un-ring a bell. You cannot un-throw a tennis ball. You cannot un-hear a speech that has already been delivered and absorbed and reacted to.

Waluigi has never respected Princess Daisy more than during this summit. She managed chaos that was not her creation. She enforced limits that should not have required enforcement. She kept the relief program on track while everything else caught fire metaphorically around her. She salvaged functional outcomes from an event that most hosts would have abandoned as unsalvageable.

Waluigi has BEEN the person trying to hold things together while everyone else panics or storms out or gives self-aggrandizing speeches. It is THANKLESS work. You do not receive credit for preventing complete disaster—you receive blame for the partial disaster that occurred despite your efforts. Daisy deserves recognition for her performance, and Waluigi is providing that recognition RIGHT NOW in this document. There. Waluigi has done his part. Someone else can handle the next decade of insufficient appreciation.

## The Peasley Problem — Legitimate Actions, Illegitimate Perception

The Peasley scandal is the part that makes Waluigi's head hurt because it is not SIMPLE and Waluigi likes things to be SIMPLE. Simple is good. Simple is 'ball goes over net, ball lands in bounds, Waluigi wins.' Simple is 'person does bad thing, person gets caught, person faces consequences.' The Peasley situation is the opposite of simple in every possible dimension.

At first examination, the scandal looked like straightforward corruption. Prince Peasley had diverted supplies secretly, bypassing normal authorization channels. That looks BAD on its face. Waluigi understands why observers were angry. If Waluigi diverted tennis equipment secretly, people would assume Waluigi was up to something nefarious. They would probably be wrong—Waluigi would be fixing a legitimate problem that nobody else noticed—but they would assume the worst because secret actions invite suspicious interpretations.

Then additional information emerged suggesting a frame-up. Fawful had intercepted communications about the supply diversion and weaponized the information politically, releasing it at maximum damaging timing. That ALSO made sense given Fawful's documented pattern of information warfare. Fawful is exactly the type of cackling menace who would intercept legitimate humanitarian logistics just to make someone look corrupt.

Then the WORST interpretive framework emerged: legitimate action handled secretly, intercepted by an enemy, twisted into a scandal that was simultaneously false and true. Peasley was not innocent—he HAD diverted supplies without proper authorization, bypassing channels that existed for accountability purposes. But he was not guilty in the way the accusations framed him—the supplies went to actual relief efforts serving genuine needs, not to his personal accounts or political allies.

Peasley did the right thing the wrong way, and his enemies made the wrong way look like proof of the wrong thing entirely.

The cost was HIGH and immediate. Loss of his title. Beanbean Kingdom threatening withdrawal from coalition structures. Public perception damage that will take years to fully remediate. And a reminder broadcast to every observer that transparency failures are INDISTINGUISHABLE from corruption during crisis periods. Even if you are doing the right thing, if you do it secretly, your enemies can make it look like the wrong thing.

Waluigi has learned this lesson personally through bitter experience. Waluigi once tried to HELP at a tennis tournament by adjusting the net height because it was clearly set incorrectly—Waluigi has an EXCELLENT eye for net heights, developed through decades of competitive play—and somehow this became 'Waluigi sabotages tournament' in the headlines. Waluigi was trying to FIX sabotage that someone ELSE had done. Did that matter? NO. Because Waluigi acted secretly instead of making a public announcement and requesting official verification of the net height discrepancy.

Perception IS reality in political contexts. Peasley forgot that or chose to ignore it because the need seemed urgent. Waluigi did not forget it—Waluigi just ignored it because the net was WRONG and someone needed to fix it immediately—but Waluigi at least UNDERSTOOD the consequences that would follow.

## The Lanky Situation — Professional Tradecraft Against an Amateur Target

Waluigi needs to defend Lanky Kong, which is not something Waluigi expected to type when beginning this entry. Waluigi did not wake up this morning thinking 'today I will write a defense of Lanky's actions.' But here Waluigi is, because the TRUTH matters and the truth is that Lanky got PLAYED by professionals while everyone blamed the amateur.

Lanky was not the CAUSE of the crisis. Lanky was the AMPLIFIER—a chaos vector identified by Kremling intelligence as someone who could be provoked, recorded looking bad, and condemned publicly. The Kremlings LEANED INTO this opportunity with professional enthusiasm and operational discipline.

They positioned objects where Lanky would encounter them awkwardly. They created interpersonal situations designed to frustrate him and make him look foolish. They had operatives ready to escalate conflicts in ways that appeared initiated by Lanky rather than by them. They documented EVERYTHING with multiple recording devices from multiple angles, ensuring comprehensive footage for post-event narrative construction. Then they released the footage as 'evidence' of Kongo Bongo incompetence and aggression.

That is not random bad luck. That is not Lanky being uniquely terrible at diplomacy. That is TRADECRAFT—professional intelligence operations executed against a target who did not realize he was a target until the trap had already closed. Classic information warfare methodology: provoke, record, condemn. The target looks bad because they WERE bad in the moment that was captured. The operator looks like an innocent victim just sharing what they observed. Even if the truth about the setup emerges later, the first narrative has already spread and taken root in public consciousness.

Waluigi has BEEN the target of this kind of operation, though not by Kremlings specifically. Wario once—in a display of entrepreneurial betrayal that Waluigi has not fully forgiven—set up an entire fake tournament specifically designed to get footage of Waluigi losing, which he then used in commercial advertising for a competing sports equipment brand. The tournament's brackets were rigged. The officiating was compromised. The entire event existed only to produce embarrassing content.

It is INFURIATING to be caught in these operations because even when you know what is happening, you cannot stop it without looking even worse. If you call out the manipulation publicly, you appear paranoid and defensive. If you ignore it and continue participating, you generate more footage for them to exploit. If you fight back directly, you give them exactly what they wanted—documentation of you being aggressive.

Lanky's mistakes were real. He DID slap a Kremling operative. That happened. The footage exists. His subsequent apology mattered and appeared genuine in its emotional content. But the narrative collapse was already underway before the slap occurred. The slap just gave the Kremlings a clean headline to attach to everything else. The systematic provocation that preceded it was the actual operation—the slap was merely the harvest.

Waluigi feels sympathy for Lanky despite not particularly knowing him. Being the person everyone points at while ignoring the actual architects of chaos is Waluigi's WHOLE LIFE EXPERIENCE. Waluigi is ALWAYS the one getting blamed while the real troublemakers skate away clean with expressions of innocent concern. Waluigi and Lanky should form a support group for people who got set up and blamed for operations they did not orchestrate.

## Comparative Analysis — Summit One Versus Summit Two

Waluigi will state this as many times as necessary until people understand: the Second Summit was BETTER than the First Summit. YES. ABSOLUTELY YES. The metrics that matter support this conclusion even if the metrics that do not matter suggest otherwise.

The first summit failed QUIETLY. Everyone smiled throughout. Everyone shook hands with appropriate warmth. Everyone expressed optimism and goodwill and positive intentions for future cooperation. The photographs looked wonderful. The press releases used words like 'productive' and 'encouraging' and 'foundation for continued dialogue.' And the summit produced NOTHING of operational value. No binding mechanisms. No logistics infrastructure. No ships launching. No programs activating. Just vibes and promises and scheduling of future meetings to discuss scheduling of other future meetings.

The second summit succeeded LOUDLY AND MESSILY. It produced ships in the water carrying supplies. It produced aid reaching refugee camps that needed assistance. It produced an eight-nation agreement with binding commitments that SURVIVED the chaos. The photographs looked tense. The press releases used words like 'challenging' and 'contentious' and 'requiring further work.' And the actual outcomes were FUNCTIONAL.

The first summit ended with optimism and no infrastructure.
The second summit ended with damaged optimism and FUNCTIONAL infrastructure.

Waluigi knows which outcome he prefers. Waluigi has participated in MANY collaborative efforts where everyone felt good about themselves and nothing actually happened. Waluigi has participated in fewer efforts where everyone felt terrible and something ACTUALLY worked. The second type is better. It just does not FEEL better, which is why people keep making the wrong comparison when analyzing these events.

Feeling good is nice. Accomplishing things is better. The Second Summit accomplished things while making everyone feel bad. The First Summit made everyone feel good while accomplishing nothing. This is not complicated mathematics.

## Reputation Outcomes — Waluigi's Assessment of Winners and Losers

**Princess Daisy:** STRENGTHENED significantly. Managed chaos she did not create. Enforced limits that should not have required enforcement. Delivered functional results while her event disintegrated around her. Best individual performance at the summit by a WIDE margin. Waluigi is not merely saying this because she is one of the few royals who has ever acknowledged Waluigi's existence and addressed him by his correct name. Waluigi is saying this because it is TRUE and Waluigi appreciates occasions when truth aligns with his opinions.

**Donkey Kong:** Bruised in short-term perception, but demonstrated leadership potential through willingness to walk out when dignity was under assault. Walking out was the RIGHT call even if the timing created cascade problems. Waluigi respects knowing when to leave. It is a skill. Most people do not possess it. They stay in bad situations because leaving feels rude. Rudeness is sometimes correct.

**Lanky Kong:** Publicly humiliated by design, privately deserving of sympathy, positioned for a redemption arc if he chooses to pursue one. Being the designated patsy is not permanent unless you allow it to become your identity. Waluigi offers this advice from extensive PERSONAL EXPERIENCE with being blamed for things.

**Captain Toadette:** Strengthened morally through demonstrated commitment to actual work, stressed politically through factional complications. Did the operational work that made the relief program function. Received less credit than she deserved. Waluigi RELATES to this dynamic deeply.

**Prince Peasley:** Politically diminished through scandal, morally complicated through methods chosen, not destroyed permanently. The arc continues. Clearing his name fully requires proving the Fawful interception chain, which is possible but requires tedious evidence compilation.

**King Dedede:** Self-inflicted catastrophe without enemy assistance required. The ONLY major figure at the summit who made things dramatically worse through purely internal decisions rather than external manipulation. Waluigi almost respects the purity of achieving failure entirely through your own efforts. Almost. Not quite. Actually not at all. Dedede is exhausting.

**Kremling Intelligence:** Short-term propaganda victory, long-term exposure risk if Funky Kong's counter-footage reaches public circulation. They played the information warfare game well but left evidence of their operation. Amateur mistake for apparent professionals.

**Meta Knight:** Not present at the summit and STILL looks more tired because of it. Waluigi has sympathy for people who inherit messes they did not create.

## The Aftermath — What Happens Now

The relief program continues operating despite everything. Ships sail on their scheduled routes. Supplies move through established channels. Refugees receive aid that they desperately need. The summit's actual PURPOSE is being accomplished even as everyone argues about scandals, speeches, slaps, and walkouts. This is the part Waluigi wants people to REMEMBER: while everyone was fighting about drama, the WORK kept getting done in the background.

Meanwhile, the Kremlings are pushing sanctions narratives through their information networks. Expect think-pieces about Kongo Bongo aggression. Expect 'concerned observers' calling for investigations that conveniently exclude Kremling provocations from scope. Expect proposals for 'neutral oversight' staffed by people sympathetic to Kremling interpretations. Waluigi has watched this playbook execute before.

Kongo Bongo faces a strategic choice: defensive isolation while the narrative hardens, or proactive narrative control through release of counter-evidence. Funky Kong apparently possesses footage that reframes the entire Lanky incident by showing the systematic provocation that preceded it. That footage is a weapon that can only be deployed effectively once—surprise and timing matter for maximum impact. They need to choose the right moment carefully, because second chances are RARE in information warfare.

Peasley's arc continues unresolved. The supplies reaching their destinations cracked the corruption narrative but did not resolve the political damage. He needs to prove the full interception chain—demonstrating that Fawful's operatives grabbed the communications mid-transit and manipulated their release timing. This requires evidence that may or may not exist in recoverable form. Possible success. Not guaranteed.

Dedede will not self-correct without external pressure applied firmly. Meta Knight knows this from direct observation. Everyone who has ever interacted with Dedede for extended periods knows this. Dreamland will probably sideline him from future diplomatic events if they possess any organizational sense, but Waluigi has observed how royal ego functions and 'sense' is often in critically short supply.

Conspiracy theories about Dreamland's Fountain of Dreams connection to the crisis have intensified because people hate invisible causation and prefer visible targets. The Fountain is the most prominent magical object associated with Dreamland. Some observers are drawing connections that may or may not be warranted. Waluigi has addressed these theories elsewhere and does not possess the energy to repeat himself here.

History will not call this summit a triumph. It will call it necessary. And in diplomacy, apparently, that is the highest compliment available when things go badly while still producing results.

Waluigi would have preferred a triumph. Waluigi ALWAYS prefers triumphs. But Waluigi will accept 'necessary and functional' if that is what circumstances offer.

WAH.

description:
Waluigi needs everyone to understand something before he describes this battle: the Vigilance was made of WOOD. It was a WOODEN ship. That FLEW. Through the AIR. And Archie Miser cast a fireball inside it. Waluigi wants that context front and center because apparently it wasn't front and center in ARCHIE'S mind when he decided to become the world's worst firefighter.

The meeting was supposed to be simple. Archie arranged to sit down with the Tea Leaf Syndicate's leadership to discuss... something. Trade? Territory? Mutual defense? Archie has never been clear about what the actual agenda was, and Waluigi suspects this is because there WASN'T one. Archie probably walked in with a vague notion of 'making friends' and a fireball loaded in the chamber just in case the friendship didn't take. That's Archie's approach to everything. Hope for the best, prepare for the worst, and define 'worst' as 'the moment when fire becomes necessary.'

The Syndicate operated out of a converted cargo hold in the lower decks. They'd decorated it with actual tea sets and comfortable furniture, because the Syndicate had CLASS. Say what you want about their criminal enterprises—and Waluigi has said PLENTY—but they understood that aesthetics matter. You can run a protection racket and still have nice curtains. Waluigi respected this about them enormously. Waluigi ALSO has excellent taste in interior decoration, which is yet another of his many underappreciated qualities.

The meeting started fine. Tea was served. Pleasantries happened. Normal diplomatic stuff that doesn't require fire.

Then someone pressed a panic button.

**The Panic Button Mystery**
Who pressed the button? GREAT question. Nobody knows. The Syndicate blamed Archie's people. Archie's people blamed the Syndicate. Some theorists think an Iron Legion operative triggered it deliberately to cause exactly the chaos that followed, which is the kind of sneaky calculated move the Legion would absolutely pull.

Waluigi has his own theory. Waluigi thinks it was an accident—someone leaned on the wrong panel, bumped the wrong switch, sat on the wrong button. Because in Waluigi's experience, most catastrophes aren't caused by evil masterminds. They're caused by someone's elbow. But the last time Waluigi shared a theory without hard evidence, he got a forty-minute lecture about 'responsible information sharing' from someone who lets ARCHIE MISER carry a spellbook. So Waluigi will keep his theory to himself. Mostly.

**The Escalation**
The panic button summoned both Toad Gang enforcers AND an Iron Legion patrol from the adjacent corridor. Within seconds, a diplomatic tea meeting became a three-faction standoff in a cargo hold. The Toad Gang came in already swinging—they heard their alarm, they showed up, they started hitting. No questions, no assessment, just fists. Waluigi admires the commitment even if he questions the strategy.

The Iron Legion troops attempted to 'establish order,' which in Legion terms means pointing weapons at everyone and demanding paperwork. Someone threw a punch. Someone drew a blade. The cargo hold turned into a blender full of angry people.

Waluigi wants to note that if HE had been handling the diplomacy, none of this would have happened. Waluigi's diplomatic approach is simple: be so magnificent that people are too impressed to fight. It has a mixed success rate, but it has NEVER resulted in a fireball.

**The Fireball**
Archie's solution to the three-way brawl was to cast a fireball.

Waluigi is going to let that sentence sit there for a moment.

A fireball. In a cargo hold. On a wooden ship. That was flying. Through the air. Full of people.

The blast killed most of the Syndicate's combat personnel instantly. Several Toad Gang and Iron Legion fighters were caught in the radius. The fact that the fireball didn't ignite the hull and send the entire Vigilance plummeting to the ground in a ball of flame is either a miracle or evidence that the universe has a sick sense of humor and wanted to see what Archie would do NEXT.

Archie has never expressed remorse about the fireball. He HAS expressed annoyance that people keep bringing it up, which tells Waluigi everything he needs to know about Archie's relationship with consequences. Waluigi makes a point of never standing within thirty feet of Archie during ANY conversation that might go badly, which, with Archie, is ALL conversations.

WAH! The man is a walking fire hazard and everyone just ACCEPTS it!
aftermath: The Tea Leaf Syndicate lost nearly all their fighters in one blast. The organization that controlled smuggling, protection rackets, and—Waluigi wants to emphasize—EXCELLENT tea distribution across the Vigilance was crippled beyond recovery. Three days later, the Syndicate Showdown finished them off entirely. The Toad Gang and Iron Legion took losses but stayed operational. Archie's reputation as someone who escalates to magical violence at the drop of a hat became a known factor that every faction had to plan around. It's like having a tornado as an ally—technically on your side, but you can't control where it goes or what it destroys. Waluigi has been on the same TEAM as Archie and he still checks for exits whenever the man reaches into his spell component pouch. WAH.

reputationNotes.archie_miser: Cast a fireball in a wooden airship, crippling the Tea Leaf Syndicate.
reputationNotes.waluigi: Expressed deep disappointment and fear towards Archie's decision-making.

name: The Syndicate Showdown
result: Tea Leaf Syndicate destroyed as an organization

casualties.attackers: One Iron Legion soldier (crushed by Green T's giant form — Waluigi saw it happen)
casualties.defenders: Earl Grey (literally exploded), remaining Syndicate forces neutralized

summary: The battle that destroyed the Tea Leaf Syndicate forever. Green T revealed he could turn into a GIANT, which Waluigi thinks he should have mentioned EARLIER. Earl Grey got poisoned by Roger's dagger and EXPLODED like a biological firework. Waluigi has seen a lot of strange things in his life but a man detonating at a marketplace was a new one.
description:
Three days after Archie's fireball gutted the Syndicate's fighting force, everyone knew it was only a matter of time before the final confrontation. Green T and Earl Grey had been trying to recruit new muscle, but the Syndicate's reputation as an organization that could protect its people had been shattered—literally—by the fireball. Nobody wanted to join the faction that just lost a fight to ONE GUY WITH FIRE MAGIC.

Waluigi actually felt bad for them, in a way. The Tea Leaf Syndicate was classy. They had standards. They served GOOD tea. In a world full of brutes and bureaucrats and fire-happy maniacs, the Syndicate represented a kind of civilized criminality that Waluigi could appreciate. You know how rare it is to find villains with aesthetic sensibility? Waluigi knows. Waluigi IS a villain with aesthetic sensibility, at least according to people who don't understand the difference between 'villain' and 'misunderstood genius.'

The confrontation kicked off in the Vigilance's mid-deck marketplace—a neutral zone where factions maintained an uneasy commercial truce. Who started it is disputed. What ISN'T disputed is that Green T decided this was where he'd make his stand, and what a stand it was.

**Green T's Transformation**
Waluigi has seen big things before. Waluigi has played sports against Bowser. Waluigi has been in the same ROOM as Petey Piranha. But when Green T transformed—when his body just EXPANDED, growing and growing until he filled the corridor like a living wall—Waluigi's jaw dropped. And Waluigi's jaw does NOT drop easily. Waluigi has a very controlled jaw.

Nobody knew Green T could do this. NOBODY. He'd been running a criminal empire with the demeanor of someone hosting a book club, and the whole time he was hiding the ability to become a COLOSSUS. The transformation froze the entire fight. Everyone—allies, enemies, marketplace shoppers who were just trying to buy apples—stopped and STARED.

Green T used those seconds of stunned silence perfectly. He brought one massive fist down on an Iron Legion soldier and the man just... crumpled. The armor folded like tin foil. It was the most dramatic display of raw physical power Waluigi had seen up to that point, and Waluigi wants everyone to know he was IMPRESSED but also SLIGHTLY OFFENDED because Waluigi has been training his whole life and this guy just GROWS? Just like that? WHERE IS THE FAIRNESS? WAH!

**Earl Grey's Spectacular Exit**
While Green T was demonstrating his new building-sized physique, Earl Grey was fighting like a man with nothing left to lose—because he WAS a man with nothing left to lose. His organization was dying around him. His boss had just turned into a giant, which probably wasn't in the employee handbook. And he was surrounded.

Roger landed a hit with his poisoned dagger. Under normal circumstances, the poison would have caused paralysis or death in the conventional, quiet, undramatic way that poisons usually work. Earl Grey's body had OTHER ideas.

The poison interacted with something in Earl Grey's physiology. Nobody has ever explained what, exactly. Some kind of alchemical compound in his blood? A latent magical instability? A tea-related mutation from years of sampling the Syndicate's more experimental blends? Whatever it was, the reaction was NOT subtle.

Earl Grey EXPLODED.

Waluigi needs to be very clear about this: he did not explode FIGURATIVELY. He did not get hit so hard he 'exploded' across the room. His body DETONATED. Outward. In all directions. The sound was somewhere between a thunderclap and a wet pop—a sound Waluigi can still hear when he closes his eyes and a sound he wishes he COULDN'T.

People ten feet away were knocked off their feet. Items and... other things... scattered across the marketplace. The vendors' stalls were splattered. Waluigi's favorite hat was splattered. WAH! That hat was CUSTOM MADE!

The explosion ended the fight. The remaining Syndicate members—those pitiful few who survived Archie's fireball AND Earl Grey's detonation—either surrendered or ran. Green T, despite his massive form, could read the writing on the wall. His organization was gone. His enforcer was, in the most literal sense possible, everywhere.

But Green T survived. That guy is RESILIENT. He went on to become one of the most important independent operators in the campaign—showing up at the Spider Grove, getting dragged into mirror dimensions, and eventually shooting a vampire lord at dinner. Waluigi has come to deeply respect Green T, partly because of his capabilities and partly because anyone who sits at a children's table plotting vampire assassination has earned Waluigi's eternal admiration.
aftermath: The Tea Leaf Syndicate ceased to exist. Its trade routes, protection networks, and excellent tea distribution all collapsed overnight. Waluigi mourns the tea most of all—the Syndicate sourced a Chamomile Midnight blend that Waluigi has NEVER been able to find anywhere else. The power vacuum aboard the Vigilance shifted hard toward the Iron Legion, who moved in on the Syndicate's former territory with the speed of bureaucrats who had been waiting for exactly this opportunity. The marketplace where Earl Grey exploded reportedly smelled strange for days. Waluigi can confirm this. It smelled like ozone and regret and something else that nobody could identify, which made it WORSE. Green T's transition to independent agent actually worked out better for him than anyone expected—freed from running an organization, he could focus on being a terrifyingly competent individual, which is what he always should have been. WAH.

reputationNotes.waluigi: Waluigi mourns the loss of tea and sees the Iron Legion as opportunistic villains.
reputationNotes.green_t: Green T's transformation secures his independence, but also ends an organization he led.

name: Battle of the Spider Grove
location: The Silent Grove, Raventree Manor Grounds
imageCaption: The Silent Grove at the height of it: the Matriarch over the egg field, and the three who went in after Eager.
result: Victory — Arachnid Matriarch banished (you are WELCOME)

attackers.name: The Party & Allies (featuring WALUIGI)
attackers.commander: Markop, assisted by THE GREAT WALUIGI & The Oracle

casualties.attackers: FNG Remi (unconscious, revived thanks to Waluigi buying time), Smoking J (bitten, venomous reaction), mechanical companion heavily damaged
casualties.defenders: Arachnid Matriarch (BANISHED via Oracle's circle), brood scattered and leaderless

summary: THIS is the one. This is Waluigi's battle. A prolonged multi-phase fight against a massive Arachnid Matriarch in the web-choked Silent Grove. Waluigi cleared paths with ice magic, weakened the Matriarch with arcane rays during the final phase, and generally held the entire operation together while everyone else was getting bitten, swarmed, or separated. The Oracle landed the finishing blow with a banishment circle, which was admittedly impressive, but Waluigi's contributions made that finishing blow POSSIBLE and he will die on this hill.
description:
The Silent Grove was the kind of place that makes sensible people turn around and walk home. Webs so thick they blocked out the sky. Egg sacs carpeting the ground like nature's worst welcome mat. Sounds from deep inside that were less 'forest ambience' and more 'something large and hungry shifting its weight.' Every instinct Waluigi had said DO NOT ENTER.

Naturally, the party walked directly in because Eager—who has a supernatural gift for finding the worst possible place to be and BEING there—had gotten himself trapped inside the spider nest. Of COURSE he had. If there's a bottomless pit within ten miles, Eager will find it. If there's a dragon's mouth within walking distance, Eager will be sitting on its tongue. The man is a MAGNET for catastrophe and Waluigi says this with a mixture of frustration and grudging affection.

Markop and Remi led the push in. Waluigi was right there with them, alongside Mossy—a Mages' Guild construct that had been 'acquired' earlier in the campaign through methods that Waluigi will describe as 'creative procurement.' Mossy was a good companion: it didn't complain, it didn't argue about strategy, and it bit things when you pointed at them. Waluigi wishes MORE of his allies had these qualities.

**Phase 1: The Rescue**
Getting to Eager meant navigating a three-dimensional maze of webbing patrolled by arachnids the size of large dogs. These things moved in PATTERNS—coordinated, deliberate, reacting to vibrations in the web network. Step on the wrong strand and three of them would come skittering from different angles. It was like playing the world's deadliest game of don't-touch-the-floor, and Waluigi is EXCELLENT at that game because Waluigi has superior agility developed through decades of competitive athletics.

Markop cut through the main web barriers with brute force. Remi's mechanical dog provided early warning when flanking spiders approached. And WALUIGI—this is the part the historians always underreport—used ICE MAGIC to freeze and shatter web clusters, opening alternative routes when the main path got too dangerous. This was DELICATE work. Too much force and the vibrations would attract the big one early. Too little and the webbing would just re-seal itself. Waluigi found the balance because Waluigi has the kind of precision that comes from years of practicing trick shots in tennis, and if you think freezing individual web strands isn't harder than a cross-court backhand, you've never tried either.

Eager was found cocooned near the grove's center, hanging fifteen feet off the ground between two dead oaks like the world's worst piñata. He was alive but completely immobilized. Getting him down required careful cutting and even more careful catching, because dropping Eager from fifteen feet onto a floor covered in egg sacs would have been catastrophic in at least three different ways.

**Phase 2: The Grove Fractures**
The rescue attracted attention. Of COURSE it did. The brood started converging from all directions and the careful, precise stealth mission became a running battle across the entire grove.

Remi and her mechanical dog held a position near a flooded stone fountain—an old structure choked with black water and dead vegetation that looked like it hadn't seen sunlight in decades. The smaller spiders probed their defensive line looking for weaknesses, testing and retreating and testing again with an intelligence that was DEEPLY unsettling. Spiders should not have tactical patience. Spiders should be small and manageable and afraid of Waluigi's boots.

Smoking J got bitten during this phase. The venom hit him FAST—swelling, disorientation, the works. He had to be pulled back from the front line, which reduced their fighting strength at exactly the wrong moment. The toad squad got cut off when a web barrier dropped behind them like a curtain—one second there was a path, the next second there was a wall of silk with toads on the wrong side of it. Communication devolved into shouted fragments across barriers of webbing and darkness.

Then the Oracle appeared, because the Oracle has a GIFT for dramatic timing. She materialized from somewhere—she was always watching from somewhere, and Waluigi finds it equal parts reassuring and creepy—and cast a massive illumination spell that turned the entire grove bright as noon. The light didn't just reveal the battlefield; it drove the smaller spiders back, buying precious seconds.

Waluigi used those seconds BRILLIANTLY. He channeled ice magic through the webbing, creating frozen corridors that the separated groups could use to regroup. The ice held the web rigid, preventing it from re-sealing, while also creating a surface cold enough to deter the spiders from crossing. It was innovative. It was effective. It was the kind of creative magical application that would get Waluigi a MEDAL in any army that appreciated talent, which is apparently NONE of them. WAH!

**Phase 3: Titan Fight**
The Arachnid Matriarch showed herself and Waluigi's stomach dropped.

She was ENORMOUS. Thirty feet across easily, her legs spanning the gaps between trees like living bridges. Her carapace was dark and ridged and scarred from fights that happened before anyone present was born. And her EYES—reflecting the Oracle's light with a cold intelligence that said this wasn't just an animal. This was something OLD. Something that had been ruling this grove for a long time and did not appreciate visitors.

Markop accepted a blessing from the Oracle—words that didn't quite sound like language, more like the noise reality makes when it bends—and grew to colossal size. COLOSSAL. Matching the Matriarch's scale. The sight of two titan-sized combatants grappling among the trees while normal-sized people scrambled between their feet was SURREAL. Waluigi has played sports in some unusual venues but running between the legs of a fifty-foot-tall friend while he wrestles a building-sized spider was a new experience even for him.

Eager, still stuck in an enlarged form from earlier events that Waluigi doesn't fully understand, contributed by spraying pepper spray on clusters of smaller arachnids. PEPPER SPRAY. On SPIDERS. And it WORKED—the capsaicin apparently disrupted whatever chemical communication the brood used to coordinate, causing them to scatter in confused circles. Waluigi has to give Eager credit for this one. It was the kind of unorthodox thinking that Waluigi appreciates because Waluigi's ENTIRE LIFE is unorthodox thinking.

The battle was then—and Waluigi cannot stress enough how ANNOYING this was—interrupted by the Vigilance flying overhead. Except it wasn't the Vigilance anymore. It was the LEGIONLANCE, under Iron Legion control, and it was broadcasting propaganda through amplified speakers. Compliance orders. Faction registration demands. BUREAUCRATIC ANNOUNCEMENTS during a GIANT SPIDER FIGHT.

Waluigi was dodging spider legs, blasting ice magic, trying not to get crushed by his own titan-sized ally, and a loudspeaker above was telling him to 'report to the nearest processing center for administrative review.' The Iron Legion's commitment to paperwork in the face of existential arachnid combat was, in its own horrible way, the most Iron Legion thing that has ever happened. WAH!

**Phase 4: The Banishment**
The final phase was DESPERATE and Waluigi is not too proud to admit it.

Remi went down. A wave of miniature spiders—hundreds of them, each barely bigger than a fist but collectively a FLOOD—swarmed over her position and she disappeared under a writhing carpet of tiny bodies. She went unconscious. Her mechanical dog fought over her prone body but was taking damage faster than it could clear the swarm.

Markop had the Matriarch in a titan-scale grapple, each of them straining against the other while trees cracked like matchsticks beneath them. But he couldn't deliver a killing blow without releasing his grip, and if he released his grip, the Matriarch would be free to do what giant spiders do to normal-sized people, which is NOTHING GOOD.

So Waluigi stepped up. WALUIGI. The guy nobody picks first. The guy who gets left off the invite list. The guy who Luigi LITERALLY pretends doesn't exist at parties. THAT Waluigi poured sustained arcane rays into the Matriarch, targeting the joints where her legs met her thorax. The magical energy burned through carapace and disrupted the internal structure keeping her upright. Each hit made her legs buckle a little more, her grip on Markop weaken a little further.

Salem—perched in the surviving trees like the world's most lethal bird watcher—landed a crossbow bolt through the Matriarch's primary eye cluster. The shot threaded through the chaos of the titan grapple and hit a target the size of a dinner plate at sixty feet. Waluigi will admit that was an INCREDIBLE shot. Waluigi is generous enough to acknowledge excellence in others, UNLIKE certain plumber brothers who shall remain nameless.

The Oracle fired an arrow into the Matriarch's abdomen carrying some kind of magical payload that made the creature convulse and shriek at a frequency Waluigi felt in his TEETH. Mossy, battered but still functioning with the mindless determination that only a construct can muster, clamped its mechanical jaws onto one of the Matriarch's rear legs and HELD ON.

The combined assault—Waluigi's arcane rays, Salem's crossbow bolt, the Oracle's enchanted arrow, Mossy's mechanical death grip—destabilized the Matriarch enough for Markop to shift the grapple. He SHOVED the massive creature backward, and the Oracle—who had been drawing a banishment circle on the ground WITH ONE HAND while fighting with the other, which is a level of multitasking that Waluigi genuinely and unreservedly respects—watched as the Matriarch crashed into the circle's boundary.

The sigils ignited. Light consumed the spider from the ground up—carapace, silk, venom, everything dissolving into brilliance. The sound wasn't a scream. It was a vibration, a frequency that Waluigi felt in his bones and his teeth and the fillings in the tooth he chipped playing baseball that one time.

Then she was gone. The grove went silent. Actually SILENT, for the first time in hours.

Waluigi stood there in the quiet, breathing hard, covered in web residue and spider ichor, and thought: THAT is why you bring Waluigi.

The loot was excellent, which helped. A War Mage's Staff that Markop claimed on Archie's behalf—and Waluigi has OPINIONS about giving Archie MORE magical firepower but nobody asked. Web-Woven Scale armor that Remi recovered once she regained consciousness and stopped screaming about the tiny spiders. And three healing potions that Rodger grabbed with the desperate speed of a man who had been counting his remaining vitality on one hand for the last hour. Waluigi didn't take any of the healing potions because Waluigi was FINE. Waluigi is ALWAYS fine. Waluigi is built DIFFERENT.

(Waluigi was not fine. Waluigi was exhausted and terrified and his hands were shaking from sustained spellcasting. But Waluigi has a REPUTATION to maintain.)
aftermath:
The party divided the Matriarch's hoard and limped back to Raventree Manor looking like they'd been through a washing machine full of cobwebs. The victory in the grove turned out to be one of the last uncomplicated wins before everything went sideways. Upon returning, the party discovered there were MULTIPLE Oracles—not one mysterious guide but several, which raised questions that made Waluigi's head hurt. Who had been guiding them? How many Oracles were there? Were they all on the same side? Waluigi doesn't trust ONE Oracle. MULTIPLE Oracles is a nightmare scenario for anyone with trust issues, which is to say, for Waluigi.

The grove victory directly preceded the Shattered Ritual and the Planar Fracture. Within twenty-four hours of banishing a giant spider, reality itself would shatter around them and Waluigi would find himself in the FEYWILD dealing with fairy court politics. In retrospect, the spider was the easy part. WAH.

reputationNotes.waluigi: Waluigi's bravery and strategic brilliance earned the Creed of Darkness' favor, while Markop's leadership drew their ire.
reputationNotes.markop: Markop's aggressive tactics during the mission caused a minor rift with the Creed of Darkness.

name: The Siege of Raventree
result: Inconclusive — The manor started fighting EVERYONE and nobody won

casualties.attackers: Unknown — wraith attacks hit the Pond Patrol perimeter hard
casualties.defenders: Green T (pulled bodily into a mirror dimension by a glass entity)

summary: Speaker L's Pond Patrol surrounded Raventree Manor after a healing attempt on Eager went wrong. Tensions were high. Arguments were had. Then the MANOR ITSELF started spawning wraiths that attacked everyone—besiegers AND defenders—because Raventree Manor is not a building, it's a HOSTILE SUPERNATURAL ENTITY that hates everyone equally. Green T got dragged into a mirror by a glass monster. Waluigi hates this house. Waluigi has ALWAYS hated this house. WAH.
description:
Waluigi knew Raventree Manor was bad news from the MOMENT he first saw it. The architecture was wrong. The shadows fell at angles that didn't match the light sources. Rooms felt larger from the inside than they looked from the outside. And the MIRRORS—every hallway had mirrors, every room had mirrors, and they all reflected things just slightly differently from what was actually there. Waluigi noticed this immediately because Waluigi spends a LOT of time looking in mirrors—for GROOMING purposes—and when a mirror shows you a version of yourself that's standing two inches to the left of where you actually are, that is NOT a grooming mirror, that is a WARNING.

But did anyone listen to Waluigi's concerns? Does anyone EVER listen to Waluigi? The answer is no. The answer has ALWAYS been no.

The siege started because of a breakdown in trust between Speaker L's faction and the people inside the manor. The failed healing attempt on Eager—details documented elsewhere because Waluigi is trying to stay focused—created a rupture. Speaker L concluded that the manor's occupants were either incompetent or hostile, and honestly, he wasn't entirely wrong about the incompetent part. His response was to surround the building with the Pond Patrol and demand answers.

From a military perspective, the Pond Patrol's encirclement was solid. Speaker L established a perimeter fifty yards from the walls, set up observation posts, controlled visible exits. The man knows how to run a siege. Waluigi will give him that. Speaker L positioned himself at the main approach and made demands through amplified address: surrender Archie for questioning, explain what happened to Eager, submit to Pond Patrol authority.

Archie, trapped inside with Hjumpik and a few others, faced limited options. No known secret exits. Outnumbered. Outgunned. So Archie surrendered himself to Speaker L, reasoning that compliance would buy time. This was either smart diplomacy or the instinct of someone who knew the manor had tricks up its sleeve that the Pond Patrol hadn't seen yet. With Archie, Waluigi has learned that the line between 'clever strategy' and 'panicked improvisation' is invisible and possibly fictional.

**The Manor Fights Back**
What happened next is why Waluigi will never set foot in Raventree Manor again. Not voluntarily. Not for money. Not even if Luigi personally BEGGED him, which Luigi would never do because Luigi doesn't know Waluigi EXISTS apparently.

Raventree Manor began to defend itself.

The building. Defended. ITSELF.

It started small. Cold spots in hallways. Shadows moving wrong. Whispers in rooms that should have been empty—not words exactly, more like the memory of words, or the threat of words, or the sound a word would make if it hated you. Then the wraiths appeared.

They came from the walls. The floors. The spaces between rooms that shouldn't have had spaces. Translucent, hostile, and—this is the important part—completely INDIFFERENT to which side anyone was on. They attacked Pond Patrol sentries on the perimeter with the same violence they directed at people inside the manor. The building didn't care about factions. It didn't care about politics. It had been provoked, and its response was to try to kill EVERYONE.

Waluigi has been in haunted houses before. Waluigi has done the haunted house event at Mario Party TWELVE TIMES. But those were haunted houses with RULES—the ghosts had patterns, the scares were predictable, and at the end you got coins. Raventree Manor had no rules. The wraiths appeared where they wanted, attacked who they wanted, and dissolved back into the architecture when they were done. You can't fight a BUILDING.

The wraiths behaved less like ghosts and more like antibodies—the manor's immune system responding to a perceived infection. The military encirclement had triggered something in the building's supernatural architecture, and that something had decided every living creature in range was a pathogen that needed to be eliminated. Waluigi finds this deeply offensive. Waluigi has excellent hygiene.

**The Glass Monster and Green T's Disappearance**
As if wraiths weren't enough—and they were PLENTY, thank you—a GLASS MONSTER crawled out of one of the manor's mirrors.

Waluigi needs to explain how disturbing this was. Imagine looking in a mirror—which Waluigi does frequently and with good reason—and instead of seeing your own magnificent reflection, you see something ELSE pushing through the glass from the other side. Something that shouldn't exist. Something made of reflections and sharp edges and wrong angles. Something that enters your world through the mirror like a hand pushing through a soap bubble, except the soap bubble is REALITY and the hand wants to GRAB YOU.

This entity was different from the wraiths. Bigger. More deliberate. It moved through the corridors with purpose—not the random hostility of the wraith antibodies, but the focused intent of something hunting a specific target.

That target was Green T.

Green T had been inside the manor when the siege started. Maybe he was investigating the supernatural phenomena independently—Green T was always investigating things—or maybe he was just in the wrong room at the wrong time. Regardless, the glass monster converged on him.

What happened next was violent and instant. The entity seized Green T and PULLED him through a mirror surface. Witnesses described it as—one moment Green T was there, fighting, his feet on solid ground. The next moment he was being dragged backward through glass that rippled like water, his expression shifting from combat focus to shock to something Waluigi doesn't want to name. Then he was gone. The mirror surface went still. It reflected nothing but an empty hallway.

Green T had been taken into what would later be identified as a mirror dimension—a layer of reflected reality that existed alongside the physical manor. The same dimensional layer that the manor's mirrors had been subtly connecting to all along. The mirrors that Waluigi had SAID were wrong. The mirrors that Waluigi had WARNED people about. But nobody listens to Waluigi about ANYTHING.

Speaker L, to his credit, maintained discipline among the Pond Patrol even as wraiths attacked his perimeter and reports came in of people being eaten by the architecture. The man has steel nerves. Waluigi respects steel nerves. But the siege's original objectives had become irrelevant. You can't negotiate a prisoner exchange with a building that's spawning ghosts and absorbing people through mirrors. The situation had outgrown politics.

The wraith manifestations eventually subsided—either the manor's defenses ran out of energy or whatever triggered them was satisfied by Green T's capture. The Pond Patrol pulled back to a safer distance but maintained observation. Nobody went inside voluntarily for a while, which Waluigi considers the first SMART decision anyone made regarding Raventree Manor.
aftermath:
Green T's disappearance into the mirror dimension set up his eventual reappearance in the Shadowfell, suggesting the mirror dimension was a transit layer between planes. This would become critical information during the Planar Fracture. The siege revealed Raventree Manor's true nature—not a building but an active supernatural entity with defenses, agendas, and the ability to devour people through its own décor. Speaker L's relationship with the manor's occupants remained badly strained. The event fed his growing conviction that conventional approaches—military, political, diplomatic—were inadequate for the threats they faced. A conviction that would deepen terribly after the Massacre at Aegis Command.

Waluigi's position on Raventree Manor, for the record, is that it should be burned to the ground. Waluigi is aware that Archie would probably volunteer for this task and that is ONE context in which Waluigi would fully support Archie's pyromaniac tendencies. WAH.

name: The Iron Sky Breach
result: Decisive Iron Legion Victory (and Waluigi is STILL mad about it)

casualties.attackers: Light — the operation was disgustingly efficient
casualties.defenders: Ship captured, crew scattered or detained; Ryan forced to jump from the airship

summary: The Iron Legion stole the Vigilance. Waluigi's HOME. The airship that everyone lived on, organized from, and relied on was seized in a coordinated boarding action and renamed the 'Legionlance,' which is a TERRIBLE name that sounds like a medical device. Ryan had to jump off the ship to survive. Bones went undercover inside the Legion. This was the worst day of the crisis until Order 120 made it look like a minor inconvenience. WAH!
description:
This battle makes Waluigi angrier than almost anything else in the entire campaign, and Waluigi is someone who maintains a COMPREHENSIVE list of things that make him angry. The Vigilance wasn't just a ship. It was where people LIVED. It was where factions met, where deals were made, where Waluigi kept his spare hats and his emergency tennis racket. The Iron Legion didn't just capture a military asset—they took people's HOME and turned it into a propaganda platform.

The Legion had been planning this for a long time. Intelligence recovered afterward showed they'd had operatives aboard for DAYS before the assault—mapping patrol routes, cataloguing defensive weaknesses, identifying where key people slept and ate and went to the bathroom. Because the Iron Legion is the kind of organization that considers 'bathroom schedules' a legitimate category of military intelligence. Waluigi finds them infuriating precisely BECAUSE they're competent. Incompetent enemies are annoying. Competent enemies are DANGEROUS. And the Iron Legion is dangerously, boringly, relentlessly competent.

The boarding launched at 16:30, timed to hit during a shift change in the Vigilance's defensive crew. Waluigi wants everyone to note that—DURING A SHIFT CHANGE. They knew the rotation schedule. They knew the exact twelve-minute window when the fewest defenders would be in position. They rehearsed this. They probably had a FLOWCHART.

Legion assault teams breached from multiple points simultaneously—cargo bay, observation deck, engine access corridors. Each team had specific objectives. Specific targets. The whole operation moved like clockwork, and Waluigi hates clockwork because it implies a world where everything goes according to someone else's plan.

The defenders were caught in the worst possible configuration. Between shifts. Scattered. Focused on external threats when the real danger was already inside the walls. The Liberated Toads had been worried about Fawful, about the Loyalists, about the factional tensions that were daily life aboard the Vigilance. Nobody had prepared for the Iron Legion to stop being 'that annoying faction that demands paperwork' and start being 'the faction that takes your ship.'

**Ryan's Jump**
Ryan's escape is the part of this story that makes Waluigi's chest tight.

Ryan was cornered on the observation deck. Legion troops closing from two directions. No other exit. And Ryan—who is braver than Waluigi will ever be, and Waluigi does not say that about many people—chose the third option.

He jumped.

Off the observation deck. Off the Vigilance. Off an AIRSHIP that was flying through the SKY.

The fall should have killed him. By any reasonable measure of physics and biology and the basic unfairness of gravity, Ryan should have died. But he didn't. Something about the angle, the air currents, hitting the tree canopy in a way that broke his fall across multiple impacts instead of one—Waluigi doesn't fully understand the mechanics and honestly doesn't want to because if he thinks about it too hard he starts hyperventilating.

Ryan survived with injuries. A Rakasha spirit-walker found him and took him in, which opened an entirely new chapter of the story. But the IMAGE—Ryan going over the railing, falling, getting SMALLER—that stays with Waluigi. Nobody should have to jump off their own home to survive. Nobody.

**Bones Goes Under**
Bones made a different choice and Waluigi respects it equally. Instead of running, Bones grabbed equipment off a fallen Legionnaire and BECAME a Legionnaire. Just like that. He stepped into the enemy's uniform, adopted their bearing, and walked through three security checkpoints on forged credentials and sheer nerve.

The disguise worked because the Iron Legion's greatest strength is also its greatest weakness: rigidity. As long as someone had the right uniform, the right papers, and followed the right protocols, the system assumed they belonged. Bones exploited this flaw brilliantly. He attended briefings. He ate in Legion mess halls. He saluted officers who would have killed him if they knew who he was. Waluigi could NEVER do this because Waluigi is too distinctive—you can't disguise six feet of purple magnificence in grey Legion armor. But Waluigi recognizes the skill.

Bones penetrated deeper and deeper into Legion territory, eventually reaching an Imperial Processing Facility. What he found inside was disturbing in ways that Waluigi does not have adequate language for. The facility treated prisoners with an industrial efficiency that stripped away personhood and replaced it with paperwork. People became case numbers. Lives became logistics problems. It was evil dressed up as administration, and it was the first clear sign that the Iron Legion wasn't just an annoying military faction—it was something much worse.

**The Legionlance**
The captured Vigilance was renamed the 'Legionlance.' THE LEGIONLANCE. Waluigi has OPINIONS about this name and all of them are negative. 'Legionlance' sounds like something you'd find in a medical supply catalogue. 'Have you tried the Legionlance for your chronic bureaucracy? Apply directly to occupied territory. Side effects may include loss of freedom, forced compliance, and having your personal belongings catalogued and stored in a sealed compartment.'

Because that's what they DID—they boxed up everyone's personal effects, labeled them, and stored them in a sealed room. The Legion DOCUMENTED everything. They probably filed a report on Waluigi's spare hats. They probably CATALOGUED the emergency tennis racket. This is what evil looks like when it has a filing system.

The Legionlance was later seen flying over Raventree Manor during the Spider Grove battle, broadcasting propaganda and compliance orders at maximum volume while Waluigi was trying to fight a GIANT SPIDER. The audacity. The absolute, bureaucratic, loudspeaker-equipped AUDACITY. WAH!
aftermath:
The Liberated Toads lost their mobile headquarters, their communications hub, and the symbolic center of their movement in a single afternoon. Without the Vigilance, they lost the ability to project force, maintain central coordination, and provide a neutral meeting ground for allied factions. Ryan was separated from everyone and picked up by a Rakasha spirit-walker. Bones went deep undercover inside Legion territory, setting the stage for the catastrophe at Aegis Command. The Iron Legion gained air superiority, surveillance capability, and a mobile command platform—advantages that no other faction could match.

Waluigi lost his spare hats, his emergency tennis racket, and a framed photograph of himself that he'd hung in his quarters. The photograph was signed. By Waluigi. To Waluigi. Because nobody else was going to do it. The Iron Legion probably filed it under 'Confiscated Personal Effects: Category W.' WAH!
